## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The rule stipulates that a lustful nun who consents to a lustful man touching her anywhere between the collarbones and the knees is expelled from the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved across all major surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahāsaṅghika versions in Chinese, the Mūlasarvāstivāda in Tibetan, and the Lokottaravāda and Sarvāstivāda in Sanskrit [SuttaCentral]. Automatic text-reuse data from DharmaNexus shows extensive phraseological overlap within the Pali canon, sharing its most substantial passages with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 2 (over 14,000 matching characters)—the monks' disciplinary rule concerning lustful physical contact—as well as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 1, Pācittiya 52, and Khandhaka treatises [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also finds cross-language alignments with Tibetan vinaya literature, including the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) and the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus].
